A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SoniDo study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison, with no material reading gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original music generation, tagging, transcription, source separation, and mixing experiments in Section 4 and Appendices B–F.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds direct Jukebox feature comparisons across several downstream tasks.

M1.justification: The hierarchical autoencoder, three autoregressive priors, CLAP conditioning, token-out augmentation, and downstream feature-injection procedures remain unchanged. Revised explanations and evaluation of Jukebox do not alter the proposed method.

E1.justification: The pretraining corpus and evaluation datasets and tasks are retained, including MusicCaps, tagging, piano and multi-instrument transcription, separation with corrupted training data, and dry/wet mixing scenarios. The expanded corpus description documents existing coverage.

E2.justification: Although Jukebox already appeared in v1's tagging and overview comparisons, v3 adds direct Jukebox comparisons for MAPS linear probing and hFT-Transformer, HTDemucs separation, and both Mix-Wave-U-Net and CRAFx2 mixing. This substantially extends comparator coverage across the central time-varying experiments.

E3.justification: Retained experiments use the same splits, preprocessing, metrics, training budgets, and data fractions. The Jukebox additions extend existing evaluation designs; Appendix E.3 explicitly uses the HTDemucs + SoniDo training settings for its Jukebox comparison.

E4.justification: Table 13 and Figure 8 extend the existing transcription data-scarcity and learning-dynamics analyses to Jukebox. Figures 13–14 also add Jukebox to separation stability and mixing training/validation analyses. These extend established analyses rather than introduce substantially new analytical questions.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and learning curves without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added Jukebox results retain this reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 3–6, 13, and 15 add substantial Jukebox results. On full-data MAPS, Jukebox achieves note F1 86.54 versus SoniDo Top's retained 86.45; HTDemucs + Jukebox achieves average SDR 6.35/6.22 on MUSDB18/MDXDB21 versus SoniDo's 8.03/7.39. Mixing scores and learning curves are also added. Table 1's replaced Jukebox separation entries should not be interpreted as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The hierarchical latent definitions, probability factorizations, and training objectives in Sections 2.1–2.2, including Equations 1–3, are retained. No substantive mathematical derivation, assumption, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The central generic-booster contribution remains, but the first introductory finding and the conclusion now explicitly refer to autoregressive models. This modestly narrows the stated model class while retaining the main downstream-performance claims.

C2.justification: The discussion extends feature-injection failure conditions to Jukebox, including HTDemucs instability and CRAFx2 overfitting in Appendix F.3. Appendix E.3 also explicitly notes that Jukebox and SoniDo used different pretraining datasets. Existing bias and sampling-rate qualifications remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly describes the existing 4,000-hour corpus as approximately 115,000 tracks, with duration and tempo ranges, 90% non-vocal content, and over 50 genres. Appendices D and E document Jukebox feature dimensions, temporal alignment, and extraction from layer 36 of the 5b model.

R1.justification: v3 adds Ma et al.'s music foundation-model survey and Comunità et al.'s SpecMaskGIT reference, removes the He et al. MAE reference, and reframes token-out's relationship to masked audio Transformers. The broader related-work discussion remains stable.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites of the introduction and experimental descriptions, clarified token-out wording, author-name corrections, and added acknowledgments. The overall section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: Existing tables gain Jukebox rows or populated entries, while Figures 6–8 and 13–14 receive corresponding labels, legends, or curves. Journal headers and some caption placements change. These are extensions within the existing visual structure.

improvement.justification: The direct Jukebox comparisons fill a relevant comparison gap and make the evidence more informative: Jukebox slightly exceeds SoniDo on full-data piano note F1 but performs worse in separation and mixing. Corpus details and narrower claims also improve transparency. The gain remains incremental because the comparisons still involve different pretraining datasets and do not isolate hierarchy as the cause of the performance differences.
